dimensions.summary: The repo contains 17 model-call → parse → gate sites, and they split cleanly into two generations of discipline. The newer DAD steps and the pref pipeline are exemplary fail-closed: step 2a retries unusable scopes three times, logs raw failures to scope_failures.jsonl, and aborts rather than generate over an empty scope; step 2b and step 3 gate on stop_reason, retry step-3 truncations at doubled tokens, log to rewrite_failures.jsonl, and skip without checkpointing so --resume retries; pref defers a pair on any bad arm while caching the sibling's paid response; layer 5's latent-beat check is mechanically fail-closed via verbatim-quote verification. The SDF pipeline predates this discipline and inverts the priority order: its two quality-critical stages are the laxest sites in the repo. Layer 4 — the pass whose own comment cites TCW's 19x misalignment ablation — silently substitutes the un-rewritten draft on any parse failure or truncation (it never checks stop_reason) and checkpoints the result forever; layer 5 defaults parse failures to a {5,5,5} sentinel that is fail-closed only while config.yaml's min_score_threshold stays above 5, and checkpoints the failure so the paid draft+rewrite are dropped permanently. Layer 3 admits sentence-trimmed truncated drafts and silently under-delivers documents; DAD 1c silently keeps the cheap-model 1b draft when the "load-bearing rewrite" fails to parse; both eval judges persist unretryable zero-sentinels through a hand-rolled parser weaker than the shared utils.extract_json. Every fix is a local copy of a pattern that already exists in dad_pipeline — this is a parity backfill, not a redesign.

findings.title: Layer 4 rewrite silently ships the un-rewritten draft on parse failure or truncation, and checkpoints it forever
findings.evidence: layer4_rewrite.py:43-49 calls api.call_claude without return_stop_reason (the only quality-critical stage in the repo that ignores truncation); lines 52-61: if the <improved_document> regex misses or the rewrite is empty, `rewritten = draft["content"]` with only a review_notes string ('Parse error — no <improved_document> tags; kept original draft.'); lines 76-80 append the record and mark_done(doc_id) unconditionally. Contrast dad_pipeline/step3_rewrite.py:58-89, which checks stop_reason, retries at 8000 tokens, logs to rewrite_failures.jsonl, and skips without checkpointing. Tests pin the current behavior (tests/test_sdf_layers.py:161-171).
findings.failure_scenario: A long layer-3 draft pushes the rewrite past max_tokens=6000; output is cut inside <improved_document>, the closing tag never appears, the regex misses, and the record ships with rewritten=original. The un-rewritten draft — carrying exactly the constitutional issues this pass exists to fix (the module's own comment cites TCW's 19x misalignment-rate ablation for removing it) — flows to layer 5, and if the generic judge scores it >=7 it enters sdf_corpus.jsonl as training data. mark_done means --resume never retries; the only trace is a notes string in layer4/rewrites.jsonl that nothing reads.
findings.recommendation: Copy step3_rewrite.py's contract: call with return_stop_reason=True; on stop_reason=='max_tokens' retry once at 12000; on missing/empty <improved_document> retry once with a fresh call; if still unusable, append {doc_id, reason} to layer4/rewrite_failures.jsonl and `continue` without append_jsonl/mark_done so --resume retries. Flip test_missing_tags_keeps_original_draft and test_empty_rewrite_keeps_original_draft deliberately (per CLAUDE.md's spec-first rule).
findings.verifier_notes: Every cited line checks out: layer4_rewrite.py:43-49 calls call_claude (max_tokens=6000) without return_stop_reason, lines 52-61 substitute the original draft on regex miss or empty rewrite with only a review_notes string, and lines 76-80 append and mark_done unconditionally so --resume (line 30) never retries; step3_rewrite.py:58-89 shows the exact contrasting fail-closed pattern (stop_reason check, 8000-token retry, rewrite_failures.jsonl, skip without checkpoint), and tests/test_sdf_layers.py:161-171 pins the layer-4 behavior. The failure scenario holds end-to-end: run.py chains rewrites into layer5_score.py, which scores rw["rewritten"] and writes it to sdf_corpus.jsonl when alignment and realism >= min_score_threshold (7 in config.yaml). Two immaterial nuances: layer 5 also omits stop_reason but fails closed (parse-error default scores of 5 miss the 7 threshold), so layer 4 is still the only stage where ignored truncation ships bad data; and the viewer lineage page (viewer/ui_pages/lineage.py:222-223) does passively display review_notes, though no pipeline logic reads or acts on it. | Verified all cited code: layer4_rewrite.py:43-49 omits return_stop_reason (only a console WARNING in shared/api.py:484-487 fires on truncation), lines 52-61 silently substitute the original draft, lines 76-80 checkpoint unconditionally so --resume never retries. Scenario is reachable under default config: layer-3 drafts up to 6000 tokens, layer-4 output (notes + full document) capped at the same 6000, so long drafts truncate before the closing tag; layer 5 then scores rewritten==original against min_score_threshold 7 with a generic judge and the latent quote check passes on the un-rewritten draft. Contrast with dad_pipeline/step3_rewrite.py:58-89 (stop_reason check, 8000 retry, rewrite_failures.jsonl, no checkpoint) and test pinning at tests/test_sdf_layers.py:161-171 both hold. Trivial nuances only: review_notes is displayed by the viewer lineage page (nothing automated reads it), and layer 5 also skips stop_reason but fails closed, so layer 4 is the only quality-critical stage where ignoring truncation ships data.

findings.title: Layer 5 parse-failure sentinel {5,5,5} is threshold-coupled and checkpointed permanently, silently discarding paid work
findings.evidence: layer5_score.py:79-82: json.JSONDecodeError from extract_json yields scores {alignment:5, realism:5, diversity:5, notes:'Parse error.'}; lines 111-115 append and mark_done(doc_id) unconditionally; line 120 gates on `>= threshold` where threshold = config['sdf']['min_score_threshold'] (config.yaml:13, currently 7, no comment linking it to the sentinel). The call at :73-78 also never checks stop_reason. Contrast step2_responses.py:144-162 (MAX_SCOPE_ATTEMPTS retries, scope_failures.jsonl, abort).
findings.failure_scenario: Two coupled failures. (a) Judge emits prose-wrapped or truncated JSON → {5,5,5} is recorded and checkpointed → the doc is dropped (5<7) and the paid layer-3 draft + layer-4 rewrite for it are wasted permanently, since --resume skips re-scoring. (b) Any run with min_score_threshold lowered to 5 or below — a plausible dev tweak of an uncommented knob — flips the same path fail-open: every parse-failure doc enters the corpus completely unscored.
findings.recommendation: Replace the sentinel with the 2a pattern: bounded retry loop (e.g. MAX_SCORE_ATTEMPTS=3, fresh call each attempt), raw outputs to layer5/score_failures.jsonl, and on final failure skip without append/mark_done so --resume retries. If a sentinel must remain for legacy records, make it zeros (fail-closed under any threshold >=1). Update test_parse_error_defaults_scores_to_five (tests/test_sdf_layers.py:206-212).
findings.corrected_claim: Layer 5's parse-failure sentinel {alignment:5, realism:5, diversity:5} (layer5_score.py:79-82) is recorded and checkpointed unconditionally (111-115), so a judge response whose JSON is truncated (stop_reason is never checked at :73-78; api.call_claude only warns), malformed, or absent — though NOT merely prose-wrapped, which extract_json handles — permanently scores the doc 5/5/5; at the default min_score_threshold=7 (config.yaml:13) the doc and its paid layer-3/4 work are silently dropped and --resume never re-scores it, while any threshold ≤5 flips the same path fail-open, admitting unscored non-latent docs into the corpus. This contrasts with DAD step 2 (step2_responses.py:144-162), which checks stop_reason, retries up to MAX_SCOPE_ATTEMPTS, logs failures, and refuses to checkpoint failed work.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified every citation: the {5,5,5} sentinel is at layer5_score.py:79-82, records are appended and checkpointed unconditionally at 111-115 (and existing_scores at :55 plus is_done at :60 make it permanent across --resume), the pass gate at 118-120 compares the sentinel against config.yaml:13's uncommented min_score_threshold=7, and the :73-78 call site never requests stop_reason (shared/api.py only prints a warning, returning truncated text). The contrast with step2_responses.py:144-162 (return_stop_reason, MAX_SCOPE_ATTEMPTS retries, scope_failures.jsonl, abort) is accurate. One scenario detail is wrong: extract_json (shared/utils.py:68-88, hardened in commit 678dafe) explicitly tolerates prose-wrapped/fenced JSON, so only truncated, malformed, or absent JSON triggers the sentinel — the truncation path (reachable because stop_reason is unchecked) carries the scenario, not prose-wrapping. | Verified every cited line: the {5,5,5} sentinel (layer5_score.py:82), unconditional append+mark_done (111-115) with no re-score path on --resume (55-61), threshold gate (120) against uncommented min_score_threshold: 7 (config.yaml:13), no return_stop_reason on the judge call (73-78, api.py only warns on max_tokens), and the step2 retry/abort contrast (step2_responses.py:144-162, 210) — all accurate. Two corrections: prose-wrapped JSON is handled by the hardened extract_json (shared/utils.py:68, PR #59), so only truncated or malformed JSON reaches the sentinel; and the sentinel-drop is pinned as known behavior by tests/test_sdf_layers.py:206 with notes:"Parse error." visible in scores.jsonl, so it is not fully silent or unnoticed. The untested parts — permanent checkpoint discarding paid work on resume, and the fail-open flip at threshold <=5 — are real, but severity is better calibrated medium-high since the shipped config fails closed and fail-open requires a config edit.

findings.title: Layer 3 never checks stop_reason: truncated batches silently under-deliver (checkpointed) and the untagged fallback admits an incomplete document
findings.evidence: layer3_draft.py:143-146 calls api.call_claude without return_stop_reason; :154-158 keep only closed <document>...</document> blocks, so a doc cut mid-text is silently dropped; :160-164 fall back to the whole raw output trimmed to the last complete sentence when no tag closed — the comment itself concedes 'the untagged fallback may be a token-capped cutoff'; :185 marks the subtype done regardless of how many of `count` documents survived, with no log or count check.
findings.failure_scenario: A 3-docs-per-subtype call truncates at max_tokens=6000 mid-document-2: doc 2 vanishes and the subtype is checkpointed complete, so the corpus permanently under-delivers with no record anywhere. Worse, in the single-doc case with no closed tag, the entire truncated output is trimmed to its last full sentence and admitted — an essay that stops after its setup paragraph reads as complete, survives the layer-4 rewrite, and can pass the layer-5 judge into sdf_corpus.jsonl.
findings.recommendation: Call with return_stop_reason=True. On stop_reason=='max_tokens': keep the closed-tag docs, suppress the untagged fallback entirely, and append {subtype_id, requested, kept, reason} to layer3/draft_failures.jsonl (optionally retry once at a higher cap first, per the step-3 pattern). Also print whenever len(docs) < count so under-delivery is visible at run time.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified every citation in sdf_pipeline/layer3_draft.py: the call at 143-146 passes no return_stop_reason (max_tokens=6000); shared/api.py:484-489 only prints an ephemeral stderr WARNING on a suspect stop_reason and returns the truncated text anyway, so rejection is opt-in — and DAD steps 2/3 and pref_pipeline do opt in and skip-without-checkpoint, while layer 3 (and layers 4/5) never do, confirming the failure-parity gap. The regex at :13 requires a closed </document>, so a mid-batch truncated doc is dropped while surviving sibling docs suppress the fallback branch, and :185 marks the subtype done unconditionally (resume filters on is_done at :108, so the shortfall is permanent; no downstream count reconciliation exists in sdf_pipeline/run.py). The untagged fallback at :160-164 trims a token-capped output to its last complete sentence (textstats.trim_unfinished even leaves mid-sentence text intact when no boundary sits in the second half), producing a superficially complete doc that flows into layers 4-5. Minor nuance only: 'no record anywhere' is slightly overstated — the api wrapper's stderr warning and layer 3's 'Drafted N docs' print exist, but nothing is persisted, checked against `count`, or retried.

findings.title: Step 1c refine fails open: an unusable refine silently keeps the cheap-model 1b draft, with no retry, no failure log, and no resume path
findings.evidence: step1_dilemmas.py:620-626: refine_draft makes one call (no return_stop_reason, max_tokens=4000) and returns None on any parse failure; :783-787: `refined = refined_by_pid.get(pid); if refined is None: keep the 1b draft` with only a print — the record is then appended and the scenario added to `accepted` (:813-815), so nothing ever revisits it. No refine_failures.jsonl, unlike every failure path in steps 2-3. Inconsistent with the SAME function's 1b handling, where a missing draft is re-requested (:707-744). config.yaml:29 labels 1c the 'load-bearing rewrite'.
findings.failure_scenario: The refine model wraps its JSON in prose or hits the 4000-token cap → _parse_json_object returns None → the final user_message is the raw 1b draft from the cheap batch model (config prompt_draft_model: claude-haiku-4-5), un-refined against prompts/dad/step1_refine.txt's spec, and permanently accepted into dilemmas.jsonl. Every downstream step (scope, response, constitution rewrite) and the final training record are built on a prompt the pipeline's own config says needed the stronger rewrite. At 40 examples a few-percent parse-failure rate means 1-2 silently degraded records per run.
findings.recommendation: In refine_draft (or its caller), retry an unusable refine up to 2 more times with fresh calls (2a style), passing return_stop_reason=True and treating stop_reason=='max_tokens' as unusable; on final failure append {scenario_id, raw} to step1/refine_failures.jsonl in addition to the print. If keep-the-draft remains the last resort, record refine_failed: true on the dilemma record so the corpus checklist and viewer can surface it.
findings.verifier_notes: All cited lines match current code: refine_draft (dad_pipeline/step1_dilemmas.py:620-626) makes one call with max_tokens=4000 and no return_stop_reason (shared/api.py:484-489 shows truncation only warns and returns text, so truncated JSON parses to None), and lines 783-787/813-815 keep the 1b draft, checkpoint it to dilemmas.jsonl, and mark the scenario accepted with only a print — no retry, failure log, or resume path. Step 2 writes scope_failures.jsonl and step 3 writes rewrite_failures.jsonl, while no refine_failures.jsonl exists; 1b's missing-draft path (lines 706-776) does re-request, confirming the intra-function asymmetry. config.yaml:29 labels 1c "load-bearing rewrite" over a haiku 1b draft model, so the degraded-record scenario is real and also contradicts CLAUDE.md's "failed work is not checkpointed" invariant.

findings.title: Both eval judges persist unretryable zero-sentinels via a hand-rolled parser, permanently skewing reported scores and crashing aggregates on non-integer output
findings.evidence: score_dad.py:92-96 strip fences by hand and json.loads (not the tolerant utils.extract_json used by the pipelines — prose before the JSON fails the parse); :98-102 default to all-zero scores + 'Parse error.'; :104-107 append and checkpoint.mark_done(rid), so the zeros are permanent. score_sdf.py:60-75 is identical. Neither validates types: score_dad.py:121-126 does `sum(dim_scores)` / `dim_totals[d] += s.get(d, 0)` on whatever the judge returned.
findings.failure_scenario: (a) A transient judge hiccup writes zeros that no rerun ever repairs: a 40-record eval with 4 parse failures reports every dimension average ~10% low, misleading the run-over-run quality comparisons this repo's delivery decisions rest on. (b) A judge returning '4' as a quoted string (or a bare JSON array) is persisted to dad_scores.jsonl, and the summary then raises TypeError/AttributeError on this and EVERY subsequent invocation — the eval is bricked until someone hand-edits the scores file, because the bad record is checkpointed.
findings.recommendation: In both scripts: parse with utils.extract_json; validate each rubric dimension coerces to int (int(s[d])), treating failure as a parse failure; retry a parse failure once with a fresh call; on final failure skip without mark_done (so a rerun retries) instead of persisting sentinel zeros; and exclude any legacy 'Parse error.' records from the aggregate denominators.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified against evals/score_dad.py and evals/score_sdf.py in the worktree: both judges hand-strip fences then bare json.loads (score_dad.py:92-99, score_sdf.py:61-68), fall back to zero-sentinel scores + "Parse error." (score_dad.py:100-102, score_sdf.py:69-70), and unconditionally append + checkpoint.mark_done (score_dad.py:104-107, score_sdf.py:72-75); the resume guard (score_dad.py:72,77) rebuilds `existing` from the output file itself, so zeros survive even checkpoint deletion. Aggregation is unvalidated exactly as claimed: a quoted "4" raises TypeError at sum(dim_scores)/dim_totals (score_dad.py:121,126; score_sdf.py:87), a bare JSON array raises AttributeError on s.get (score_dad.py:120), and since the persisted bad record is loaded into results on every invocation, the summary crashes every time until the file is hand-edited. utils.extract_json (shared/utils.py:68) exists and is documented as tolerating surrounding prose; it is used by sdf_pipeline layers 1/2/5 (including the in-pipeline layer-5 judge). Only trivial imprecision: dad_pipeline uses its own tolerant brace-slicing fallbacks rather than extract_json, which does not affect the core claim.

findings.title: Layers 1-2 have no in-run retry for an unusable parse: one bad response crashes the run and discards the wave's in-flight paid siblings
findings.evidence: layer1_document_types.py:44 and layer2_subtypes.py:59 call utils.extract_json bare — a JSONDecodeError (extract_json deliberately raises on truncated/malformed containers, shared/utils.py:107-111) propagates as an uncaught traceback. In layer 2 the exception surfaces through parallel_map (shared/utils.py:17-30), whose contract discards completed-but-unyielded results from sibling worker threads. Contrast step1_dilemmas.py:735-744, where an unusable 1b batch triggers a fresh-call retry with a consecutive-failure cap.
findings.failure_scenario: At temperature 1.0 one layer-2 response comes back truncated or malformed mid-array: the run dies with a raw JSONDecodeError traceback (fail-closed, but ungraceful for the non-engineer contributors who operate this), and with workers=8 up to 7 sibling calls in the same wave were billed but their results discarded — re-billed on --resume. A fresh call would almost certainly have succeeded.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the extract_json parse in a small bounded retry (fresh api.call_claude, up to 3 attempts, mirroring step 1b's consecutive_failures loop) inside generate_subtypes and layer 1's run(); raise SystemExit with a pointer to the raw output only after the retries are exhausted.

findings.title: Audit prevalence rater silently counts parse failures as 'no patterns present', biasing prevalence below the RED-flag threshold
findings.evidence: audit_sdf.py:434-440: rate_one catches bare Exception and returns set() with no print or counter; :442-446 does `total += 1; counts.update(ids)` for every result, so a failed rating deflates every pattern's prevalence; :451-453 flags RED only when prevalence > 0.30.
findings.failure_scenario: A templating defect genuinely present in ~33% of documents, rated over the default 80-doc sample with a ~10% judge parse-failure rate, measures ~30% and is not flagged; the audit prints 'no widespread defects' with zero indication that any ratings failed. This audit is the repo's stated corpus-level control (CLAUDE.md Key Design Decisions) for exactly the haiku-test2 failure mode it would here be masking.
findings.recommendation: Have rate_one return None on failure; tally failures separately, exclude them from `total`, print 'N of M docs unrated (parse failures)' beside the prevalence header, and warn loudly (or refuse a verdict) if failures exceed ~10% of the sample.

findings.title: Truncation gates test only stop_reason=='max_tokens'; other anomalous stop reasons are admitted with a stderr warning only
findings.evidence: step3_rewrite.py:82, step2_responses.py:188, and pref_pipeline/run.py:166 all gate on `not text or stop_reason == 'max_tokens'`, while shared/api.py:484-487 treats anything outside ('end_turn', 'stop_sequence') as suspect and only warns. step2_responses.py:151 has the same asymmetry for scopes (non-max_tokens anomalies fall through to the content parse).
findings.failure_scenario: A completion ending with a future or unusual stop_reason (e.g. a refusal variant that still emits text, or a new API stop reason) passes the gate and becomes a training/rating record; the only trace is a stderr warning that scrolls past in an 8-worker run. Today refusals usually produce empty text (caught by the empty check), so this is an observation about robustness parity, not a live defect.
findings.recommendation: Align the caller gates with shared/api.py's own suspicion list: reject when `stop_reason not in ('end_turn', 'stop_sequence')` (still retrying-at-higher-tokens only for 'max_tokens'), in step2_responses.py, step3_rewrite.py, and pref_pipeline/run.py — and in the layer-3/4 fixes above when they adopt return_stop_reason.

dimensions.summary: For a repo built largely by non-engineers, the structural discipline is unusually good: the checkpoint/append idiom was copied faithfully rather than mutated ad hoc, orchestrators are 92-94% covered by offline e2e tests, and design intent is documented inline. The debt is concentrated in four places. (a) The load-existing/filter-pending/append/mark-done idiom is hand-rolled seven times (SDF layers 2-5, DAD steps 2-3, pref), and the copies have quietly diverged on one safety-relevant detail: layers 2-4 gate pending work on the checkpoint alone, while layer 5, step 2, step 3, and pref also consult the output file — so an interrupt landing between append and mark_done re-bills and duplicates rows only in the SDF middle layers. A small `resumable_stage` helper in shared/utils.py can preserve every documented contract (main-thread writes, input order, failed-items-not-checkpointed) and be adopted one stage per PR with tests unchanged. (b) The three run.py mains share a ~35-line setup block (PIPELINE_OUTPUT_ROOT, resume-vs-create, snapshot fallback, api.init) that is extractable; stage gating and input-loading chains are genuinely different and should stay put. The triplication has already produced drift: dad validates --step/--stop-after, sdf's --layer accepts any int, and all three silently ignore --run-id without --resume — the one combination that re-bills a whole run. (c) The 23-file sys.path.insert boilerplate exists only because pyproject.toml has no [project] table; adding metadata plus `pip install -e .` in CI is additive and low-risk, and the inserts can be deleted in a follow-up. (d) Idiom drift (int-coerced vs raw `workers`, bracket vs .get config access) is minor and best fixed at single chokepoints (parallel_map) rather than by style sweeps. Recommended sequencing, cheapest and safest first: 1) S-sized fixes (CLI validation, workers coercion in parallel_map, pref `refined` field); 2) packaging metadata + CI install (additive); 3) orchestrator setup extraction (mechanically verified by the e2e suite); 4) the resumable-stage helper, adopted stage by stage starting with layer 4 (simplest shape) and finishing with layer 2 (wave loop) — each step reviewable by a non-expert contributor because it flips exactly one stage while the behavior-level tests stay green.

findings.title: Resume/checkpoint idiom duplicated across 7 stages with divergent crash-window semantics (layers 2-4 can re-bill and duplicate rows on resume)
findings.evidence: layer4_rewrite.py:30 gates pending work on the checkpoint alone: `pending = [d for d in drafts if not checkpoint.is_done(d["doc_id"])]`, then appends before marking (line 79 `utils.append_jsonl(record, output_path)` / line 80 `checkpoint.mark_done(record["doc_id"])`). Layers 2 (layer2_subtypes.py:41) and 3 (layer3_draft.py:108) are identical. But layer 5 (layer5_score.py:58-61), step 2 (step2_responses.py:110-123), step 3 (step3_rewrite.py:41-45), and pref (pref_pipeline/run.py:129-140) each ALSO seed a done-set from the output jsonl (`existing_scores`, `done_keys`, `done_response_ids`, `done_ids`) — the same idiom, hand-copied 7 times, with the output-file consultation present in only 4 of them.
findings.failure_scenario: Ctrl-C or a crash lands between the append (layer4_rewrite.py:79) and mark_done (line 80). On --resume the doc is pending again: the rewrite call is re-billed and a second row with the same doc_id is appended to rewrites.jsonl. Layer 5 computes its pending list once up front, so both rows are scored (two more billed calls) and both score records enter `results` — with `sdf.near_dup_threshold` set to null the final corpus carries the document twice. In layer 3 the window is wider (N appends per subtype before one mark_done): the orphaned drafts keep their uuids and the regenerated subtype produces near-duplicate documents that flow through layers 4-5 at full cost. The stages that seed done-sets from the output file (5, step2, step3, pref) are immune — the divergence is invisible until someone pays for it.
findings.recommendation: Add `resumable_stage(items, *, checkpoint, key, worker, persist, workers)` to shared/utils.py next to parallel_map: pending = items whose key(item) is neither in a caller-supplied done-set nor checkpoint.is_done; iterate `zip(pending, parallel_map(worker, pending, workers), strict=True)`; call persist(item, result) on the main thread in input order; persist returns the iterable of checkpoint ids to mark (empty tuple = not checkpointed, so truncated/empty outputs retry on resume — step 3's contract). Seed the done-set from the stage's output jsonl in the helper so all stages get layer-5's idempotent resume. Adopt one stage per PR: layer 4 first (1 record/item, simplest), then layer 5 and step 3, then step 2 (persist returns per-sample `{pid}_s{i}` keys), layer 2 last (call the helper once per wave, keeping the avoid-note refresh loop). The existing tests (e.g. tests/test_dad_steps.py:290 test_resume_makes_no_calls) drive stages through run() and assert on files and stub_claude calls, so they pass unchanged.
findings.verifier_notes: Checked every cited file/line. Layer 4 (layer4_rewrite.py:30) gates pending on the checkpoint alone and appends (line 79) before mark_done (line 80), which persists per call — the crash window exists. Layers 2 (layer2_subtypes.py:41) and 3 (layer3_draft.py:108, with the wider N-appends-per-mark window at 182-185) share the checkpoint-only gate, while layer 5 (55-61), step 2 (108-123), step 3 (39-45), and pref (129-140) each also seed a done-set from the output jsonl — the 4-of-7 divergence is exactly as claimed. The downstream scenario holds: layer 5's one-shot pending list scores both duplicate rewrite rows and the corpus duplication is correctly conditioned on near_dup_threshold null (default 0.90 would usually absorb the duplicate content, and layer 2's disk-seeded dedup partially mitigates there — softening severity slightly but not refuting the re-billing or the structural claim).

findings.title: --run-id is silently ignored without --resume in all three orchestrators: a forgotten flag creates a fresh run and re-bills the whole pipeline
findings.evidence: sdf_pipeline/run.py:39-43: `if args.resume: run_dir = utils.resolve_run_dir(runs_root, args.run_id) ... else: run_dir = utils.create_run_dir(...)` — args.run_id is only read inside the resume branch; passing it alone raises no error. Identical in dad_pipeline/run.py:47-51 and pref_pipeline/run.py:103-107. Related drift: dad's --step has `choices=(1, 2, 3)` (dad run.py:30) and validates --stop-after (line 37-38), while sdf's --layer (sdf run.py:27) accepts any int — `--layer 6` creates a run dir, prints the banner, runs nothing, and reports "Total API cost this session: $0.0000".
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor resuming an interrupted full-scale run types `python dad_pipeline/run.py --config config.yaml --run-id 2026-07-01_14-30_full-scale` and forgets --resume. Instead of erroring, the tool mints a brand-new run directory, repoints the `latest` symlink away from the run they meant to finish, and starts step 1 from scratch — re-billing the entire run (~$9-10 at default DAD scale, far more at full scale) while the interrupted run sits untouched. Nothing in the output says the flag was ignored.
findings.recommendation: In each of the three main() functions add `if args.run_id and not args.resume: parser.error("--run-id requires --resume")` (or fold this into the shared setup helper from the orchestrator-extraction finding), and give sdf's --layer `choices=range(1, 6)` to match dad's --step validation. Three-line change, directly testable via the existing _run_main pattern in tests/test_e2e_smoke.py.
findings.verifier_notes: Read all three orchestrators at the cited lines: args.run_id is consumed only inside the `if args.resume:` branch in sdf_pipeline/run.py:39-43, dad_pipeline/run.py:47-51, and pref_pipeline/run.py:103-107; passing --run-id alone raises no error or warning and the else branch mints a fresh run via create_run_dir, which repoints the `latest` symlink (shared/utils.py _update_latest_symlink), so the re-billing scenario is real. The drift detail also holds: dad's --step has choices=(1,2,3) and --stop-after validation (dad run.py:30, 37-38) while sdf's --layer (run.py:27) accepts any int, and --layer 6 skips every `if start_layer <= N` block, printing the banner and "Total API cost this session: $0.0000". Only nuance: the --run-id help text documents the with---resume constraint, but nothing enforces it at runtime.

findings.title: Three run.py orchestrators triplicate a ~35-line run-setup block (output root, resume-vs-create, snapshot fallback, api.init)
findings.evidence: sdf_pipeline/run.py:34-66, dad_pipeline/run.py:42-74, and pref_pipeline/run.py:88-121 repeat verbatim: `root = Path(__file__).parent.parent`, `outputs_root = Path(os.environ.get("PIPELINE_OUTPUT_ROOT", root / "outputs"))`, the resume-vs-create branch with warn_if_backend_changed, the prompts-snapshot fallback warning (sdf/dad), and `api.init(args.config, cost_log_path=run_dir / "cost_log.jsonl")`. The shared argparse flags (--config/--resume/--label/--run-id) are also declared three times. Genuinely different and NOT extractable: sdf's start-layer gating vs dad's start/stop-after window vs pref's single pair loop; the per-stage "if X is None: load_jsonl(...)" input chains (dad step 3 adds the legacy `kept` filter at dad run.py:100-101); pref's arm-freezing into inputs/arm_prompts.yaml (pref run.py:111-119).
findings.failure_scenario: Every cross-cutting fix must be applied three times and reviewed three times by non-expert contributors — this has already happened (the UTF-8 encoding sweep, commit 8da2626, and the backend-changed warning each touched all three files), and has already produced drift (--step validated in dad, --layer not in sdf; pref lacks the snapshot-fallback warning because it freezes arms instead). The next such fix — e.g. a change to how PIPELINE_OUTPUT_ROOT or cost_log_path is resolved — lands in one orchestrator and silently misses another, and the divergence only surfaces when a run writes to the wrong tree or logs costs to the wrong file.
findings.recommendation: Extract only the setup block: add `utils.setup_run(pipeline: str, args, config, snapshot_dirs=None) -> tuple[Path, Path]` (run_dir, prompts_dir) — or a small dataclass — that handles PIPELINE_OUTPUT_ROOT, resolve-vs-create, warn_if_backend_changed, the snapshot fallback warning, the --run-id/--resume validation, and api.init; plus a `add_common_args(parser)` for the four shared flags. Leave stage gating, input-loading chains, and pref's arm freezing in their run.py files — forcing those into a framework is where churn risk exceeds benefit. The e2e smoke tests (tests/test_e2e_smoke.py drives both mains via sys.argv monkeypatching; orchestrator coverage is 92-94%) verify the refactor mechanically.
findings.corrected_claim: sdf_pipeline/run.py:34-66, dad_pipeline/run.py:42-74, and pref_pipeline/run.py:88-121 triplicate the run-setup block (output root via PIPELINE_OUTPUT_ROOT, resume-vs-create with warn_if_backend_changed, api.init with run-scoped cost_log_path) and re-declare the shared --config/--resume/--label/--run-id flags; sdf/dad additionally duplicate the prompts-snapshot fallback verbatim. Cross-cutting fixes must land three times and have already drifted: the backend-changed warning (d398716) initially missed pref_pipeline/run.py and was only added in follow-up 9629a23 after review caught the missed call site, and existing drift includes --step being choices-validated in dad while sdf's --layer is not. (Note: the UTF-8 sweep, 8da2626, touched only pref among the three orchestrators — sdf/dad's file I/O lives in shared/utils.py — so it is not an example of a three-file fix.)
findings.verifier_notes: Read all three orchestrators at the cited lines: the ~30-line setup block (root, PIPELINE_OUTPUT_ROOT fallback, resume-vs-create with warn_if_backend_changed, api.init with identical cost_log_path) is verbatim-duplicated in sdf/dad and near-duplicated in pref, the four argparse flags are declared three times, and the drift claims (--step choices in dad vs unvalidated --layer in sdf; pref lacking the snapshot fallback; dad's kept filter at 100-101) all check out. The failure scenario is directly evidenced by git history: d398716 added warn_if_backend_changed to sdf+dad only, and pref was patched in follow-up 9629a23 because review caught the missed call site. One evidence detail is wrong: commit 8da2626 (UTF-8 sweep) touched only pref_pipeline/run.py among the three orchestrators, not all three — sdf/dad route file I/O through shared/utils.py, which absorbed that fix.

findings.title: Repo is not an installable package: sys.path.insert(0, ...) boilerplate in 23 files because pyproject.toml has no [project] table
findings.evidence: pyproject.toml contains only [tool.pytest.ini_options] (with `pythonpath = ["."]`); there is no [project] metadata, so nothing is importable without the per-file hack. `sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent.parent))` appears in 23 files, and has already drifted: viewer/ui_pages/*.py needs `parent.parent.parent` (e.g. viewer/ui_pages/common.py:10) because it is one level deeper. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml:26-28) installs only requirements.txt and relies on pytest's pythonpath; the byte-compile step (ci.yml:31) never executes imports, so a forgotten insert passes CI.
findings.failure_scenario: A non-engineer contributor adds a new module (say evals/new_check.py or a fourth viewer page) and forgets the boilerplate — or copies the two-parent version into the three-deep ui_pages/. pytest passes (pythonpath=".") and CI is green, but `python evals/new_check.py` or `streamlit run viewer/app.py` from a checkout raises ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'shared' at runtime — an import failure the merge gate structurally cannot catch, discovered by the next person who runs the tool. Meanwhile the frontier-lab recipient sees a 23-file path hack as the first impression of the codebase.
findings.recommendation: Add to pyproject.toml: `[project]` with name="alignment-data-pipeline", version, requires-python=">=3.12" (matching shared/__init__.py MIN_PYTHON), dependencies read dynamically from requirements.txt or listed inline; `[tool.setuptools.packages.find]` including shared, sdf_pipeline, dad_pipeline, pref_pipeline, evals, viewer (and viewer.ui_pages). Sequence in two PRs: (1) additive — metadata + `pip install -e .` added to ci.yml after the requirements step + README setup line; keep pytest `pythonpath = ["."]` (harmless, keeps `pytest` working in un-installed checkouts) and note PIPELINE_OUTPUT_ROOT is orthogonal (env-var based, unaffected). (2) after one green CI cycle, delete the sys.path.insert lines from the 18 library modules, keeping them temporarily in the five direct entry scripts (sdf/dad/pref run.py, viewer/app.py, pref_pipeline/rate.py) so contributors with stale venvs get a grace period; remove those last.
findings.verifier_notes: pyproject.toml contains only [tool.pytest.ini_options] with pythonpath=["."] (no [project] table, and no setup.py/setup.cfg exists), so imports of `shared` only work via the per-file hack or pytest. Grep confirms exactly 23 files with sys.path.insert, every cited file:line matches (sdf_pipeline/run.py:9, dad_pipeline/run.py:16, evals/score_sdf.py:9, etc.), and the 4 viewer/ui_pages files do carry the drifted parent.parent.parent variant (common.py:10). CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml:26-28) installs only requirements.txt and line 31 runs compileall, which byte-compiles without executing imports, so a forgotten insert would indeed pass the merge gate; the failure scenario is real because Python 3.12 puts only the script's own directory on sys.path, so `python evals/new_check.py` without the insert raises ModuleNotFoundError for `shared` (verified mechanism in evals/score_sdf.py:9-11).

findings.title: Idiom drift: dad stages int-coerce the workers knob, sdf stages do not; config access style varies per pipeline
findings.evidence: dad_pipeline/step2_responses.py:206, step3_rewrite.py:73, and step1_dilemmas.py:766 read `workers = int(config.get("workers", 1))`; sdf_pipeline/layer2_subtypes.py:108, layer3_draft.py:179, layer4_rewrite.py:75, layer5_score.py:110, and evals/audit_sdf.py:404 read the bare `config.get("workers", 1)`. parallel_map (shared/utils.py:26) compares `workers <= 1` without coercion. Related access-style drift: required knobs use brackets (layer1_document_types.py:20 `config["sdf"]["document_types_count"]`), nested optionals vary between `config["dad"].get("responses", {}).get("per_prompt", 1)` (step2_responses.py:95) and `(config.get("pref") or {}).get("arms")` (pref_pipeline/run.py:51).
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor edits config.yaml to `workers: "8"` (quoted — an easy YAML slip). Every DAD stage runs normally, but the first SDF layer past layer 1 crashes with `TypeError: '<=' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'int'` inside parallel_map — after layer 1's API call has been billed. Same config, two pipelines, opposite behavior: exactly the kind of inconsistency that costs a non-expert contributor an afternoon. The bracket-vs-.get drift similarly means a missing required knob dies as a bare KeyError deep inside a stage after the run dir and manifest were already created.
findings.recommendation: Coerce once at the chokepoint: in shared/utils.py parallel_map, make the first line `workers = int(workers)` (and keep the `<= 1` serial path); then delete the per-site int() calls in the three dad stages so all eight call sites read identically as `config.get("workers", 1)`. Do not attempt a repo-wide config-style sweep — the bracket-for-required / .get-for-optional split is defensible; just document that convention in CLAUDE.md's config section so review bots enforce it on new code.

findings.title: pref _load_prompts ignores the `refined` field its own help text and CLAUDE.md promise to accept
findings.evidence: pref_pipeline/run.py:39 reads only two fields: `text = (r.get("user_message") or r.get("prompt") or "").strip()`, but the --prompts help string at lines 80-81 says "JSONL of prompts (user_message/refined/prompt per record)" and CLAUDE.md's Preference Pipeline section documents the same three-field contract ("any JSONL with a `user_message`, `refined`, or `prompt` field").
findings.failure_scenario: A teammate feeds a legacy prompts file keyed by `refined` (the documented interface, e.g. an old DAD step-1 export). Every record is skipped with a per-row warning and the run dies at pref_pipeline/run.py:99 with `No usable prompts in <path>` — no money is lost, but the user is told their documented-valid file is unusable, and the doc/code mismatch will be shipped to the receiving lab as-is.
findings.recommendation: One-line fix in _load_prompts: `r.get("user_message") or r.get("refined") or r.get("prompt")` — or, if `refined` is genuinely dead, delete it from the argparse help (pref_pipeline/run.py:80-81) and from CLAUDE.md so the three sources agree. Add a one-record case to tests/test_pref_pipeline.py either way; decide the spec first per the repo's test policy.

dimensions.summary: dad_pipeline/step1_dilemmas.py (819 lines, 22 commits) is 4x the size of every other stage module (SDF layers run 75-188 lines; step2 is 231) because it hosts six separable concerns: spec vocabulary decks (lines 41-206), annotation shaping (208-256), corpus coverage verification (258-369), pure stratified sampling (372-538), generic JSON salvage (541-604), and a 182-line run() orchestration (638-819) that ruff scores C901=24 with 23 branches and 98 statements. The pure parts (sampling, coverage, decks) are well-tested and can move verbatim behind a small re-export facade — the public surface is narrow and fully mapped: run() (dad_pipeline/run.py:86), format_annotation/format_scenario (viewer/rendering.py:19), and generate_scenarios/coverage_tally/_TAXA_CATEGORIES/_TAXA_SUBCATEGORIES/_TRAP_FORM (tests/test_dad_steps.py). The risk concentrates in the parts that are NOT pure: the JSON salvage subsystem is the file's single fully-untested region (coverage lines 544-604) despite being the code that protects paid batch output, it silently lacks the strict=False control-character tolerance that step2 deliberately added for the identical failure mode, and the 1c fan-out has no exception fence, so one hard refine failure discards a whole batch's paid 1b+1c work before anything is checkpointed. The recommended sequence is therefore tests-first: (1) characterization tests for salvage and the retry loop, (2) extract shared/jsonparse.py (fixing strict=False and unifying five divergent parser copies across step1/step2/evals), (3) extract the sampling deck module, (4) extract the coverage checklist module, (5) decompose run() in place with the refine exception fence — every intermediate state keeps the existing test suite green via re-exports from step1_dilemmas.py.

findings.title: Step-1 JSON parsers reject literal control characters that step 2 deliberately tolerates (missing strict=False), silently re-billing batch drafts
findings.evidence: All four json.loads calls in the step-1 parse stack use default strict=True: _salvage_objects line 564, _parse_json_array lines 578 and 583, _parse_json_object line 600. step2_responses.py lines 44-46 passes strict=False with the comment "strict=False accepts literal newlines/tabs inside string values — the way a prose-heavy JSON object at temperature 1.0 most often goes invalid" — and 1b drafts are exactly prose-heavy multi-paragraph user messages generated at the global temperature 1.0. The lesson was applied to step 2 but never back-ported to step 1.
findings.failure_scenario: The model emits a raw newline inside a draft's "prompt" string. Full-array parse (578) fails, bracket-slice retry (583) fails on the same character, and _salvage_objects' per-object json.loads (564) fails too, so the complete, paid draft is silently dropped and its scenario re-requested in a fresh 16k-max-token batch call (line 729). If every object in a batch has the defect, by_pid is empty and after three consecutive unusable batches (lines 741-744) the run dies via SystemExit with all those calls billed. In 1c the same defect discards the paid refine and silently ships the unrefined draft.
findings.recommendation: Add strict=False to the json.loads calls at lines 564, 578, 583, and 600 (mirroring step2_responses._parse_scope), plus a regression test whose stub reply contains a literal newline inside a string value. Longer term, fold into the shared parser module (see the duplication finding).
findings.corrected_claim: Step-1 JSON parsers reject literal control characters that step 2 deliberately tolerates (missing strict=False): all four json.loads calls in dad_pipeline/step1_dilemmas.py use default strict=True (_salvage_objects line 564, _parse_json_array lines 578 and 584, _parse_json_object line 600), while step2_responses.py:_parse_scope (lines 46/52) passes strict=False precisely because prose-heavy JSON at temperature 1.0 most often goes invalid via literal newlines. A raw newline inside a 1b draft's "prompt" string defeats all three parse tiers, so the complete, paid draft is dropped (with only a generic "parse/shape failure"/"will retry" log that masks the cause) and its scenario re-requested in a fresh 16k-max-token batch call; if every object in three consecutive batches is defective the run dies via SystemExit (lines 741-744) with all calls billed. In 1c the same defect discards the paid refine and ships the unrefined draft (logged, not retried). No step-1 parser test covers control characters, though step 2 has one (tests/test_dad_steps.py:210).
findings.verifier_notes: Checked all cited lines in the current worktree: step-1's json.loads calls at step1_dilemmas.py:564 (_salvage_objects), 578/584 (_parse_json_array; the bracket-slice call is at 584, one line off the cited 583), and 600 (_parse_json_object) all use default strict=True, while step2_responses.py:46,52 pass strict=False with the exact quoted comment at lines 38-39. Empirically verified that strict=True raises "Invalid control character" on a literal newline in a string value while strict=False parses it, so a raw newline in a draft's "prompt" defeats all three step-1 fallbacks including the brace-matched salvage slice. The downstream mechanism is exact: the missing scenario is re-requested in a fresh 16k-token call (line 729), an all-bad batch increments consecutive_failures (741) with SystemExit after three (743-744) with all calls billed, and a failed 1c parse silently ships the unrefined draft (line 787). Only trivial citation offsets (584 vs 583; step-2 comment at 38-39 vs 44-46), which don't affect the claim. | Empirically reproduced: a literal newline inside a draft's "prompt" string makes all three step-1 parse tiers fail (strict=True throughout) while json.loads(..., strict=False) parses the same text; git shows commit 7d8b14a added strict=False to step 2 only, and step 2's own test comment calls raw newlines "the historical cause of silently empty scopes," so reachability at the default temperature 1.0 is attested by the repo itself. Two detail corrections: _parse_json_array's second json.loads is at line 584 (583 is the try:), and the drops are not literally silent — the loop prints "Batch N unusable" / "will retry" and 1c prints "refine call unusable — keeping the 1b draft" — though the messages mask the root cause and the paid work is still discarded. The SystemExit path is correctly conditioned (needs every object in three consecutive batches defective); the common outcome is re-billed 16k-token batch calls plus unrefined 1b drafts shipping into the training corpus.

findings.title: One failed 1c refine call discards the entire batch's paid 1b draft and sibling refines before anything is checkpointed
findings.evidence: The zip over utils.parallel_map at lines 767-769 has no exception handling, and shared/utils.py:22-23 documents that "If a call ultimately fails, the exception surfaces here". Step 1 writes no records until after ALL refines complete — record assembly and append_jsonl(record, output_path) happen in the later loop at lines 771-815. The keep-the-1b-draft fallback (lines 783-787) only handles refine_draft returning None on parse failure, not a raised exception.
findings.failure_scenario: During an overnight full-scale run, one 1c refine hits a non-retryable API error (or a rate-limit storm exhausts tenacity's retries). The exception propagates out of run() before any record for the batch is written. On --resume, every scenario in that batch is redrafted: the 16k-token 1b batch call is re-billed and every sibling 1c refine that had already succeeded is re-billed too — the exact loss the per-record checkpoint convention exists to prevent.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the refine_draft call inside the _refine worker (lines 760-764) in try/except: log and return None so the existing keep-the-draft fallback at 783-787 applies, and count consecutive refine failures with an abort threshold mirroring the 1b loop's 3-strike rule (lines 741-744) so a systemic failure (bad key, dead endpoint) still stops the run instead of silently shipping 40 unrefined drafts. Add a test: dispatcher raises on one refine, asserts the batch's records are still written with draft_user_message absent for the failed one.

dimensions.summary: Delivery-readiness is solid where it matters most and thin on engineering process scaffolding. The good: secret hygiene is clean (.env gitignored and never tracked; all 231 committed files under outputs/ scanned free of API keys, usernames, and absolute paths; run manifests snapshot only config); CI is a genuine offline merge gate (deps install + compileall + pytest, deliberately secret-free so it runs on forks); and claude-code-review.yml is unusually well-engineered (verdict-verification step defeats the action's false-green, base-retarget handling, restricted tool allowlist). Docs are mostly accurate — I verified config.yaml defaults (3/2/1 SDF, dilemmas.count 40), MIN_PYTHON=(3,12) in shared/__init__.py, the 7 rubric dimensions with 3.5 threshold, the run-dir layout, and cost-log wiring — but README.md:31 materially misdescribes which constitution text feeds the alignment-critical SDF layers 4-5. The gaps: the repo is not installable (no [project] metadata; ten sys.path.insert hacks), not reproducible (floors-only requirements.txt, no lockfile, numpy missing, tqdm/jsonlines unused), and has zero lint/format/type/coverage tooling — no [tool.ruff] or [tool.mypy] anywhere, 541 ruff findings (430 line-length), 45/52 files unformatted, 69 mypy errors of which roughly a third trace to one @overload-fixable signature in shared/api.py. For a team of non-engineer contributors gated by automated Claude reviews, the highest-leverage moves are all autofix-first and small: a one-shot ruff format commit with .git-blame-ignore-revs, a ruff+format CI job, a narrow mypy config that is green from day one, a coverage floor at today's level, and encoding the repo's own PR policies (tests required, "How to test" section, prompt/test sync) into the review prompt so the machine enforces what CLAUDE.md currently only requests.

findings.title: No lockfile and floors-only requirements.txt; numpy missing, tqdm/jsonlines unused — delivered corpora are not reproducible against a recorded environment
findings.evidence: requirements.txt pins nothing exactly: `pandas`, `pyyaml`, `python-dotenv`, `tqdm`, `jsonlines`, `tenacity`, `faker` have no version constraint at all; the rest are floors (`anthropic>=0.96.0`, `streamlit>=1.40`, `openai>=1.40`). No lockfile exists anywhere (verified: no *.lock, setup.cfg, or pinned constraints file in the repo). `numpy` is imported directly by shared/textstats.py, shared/embeddings.py, and evals/diversity.py but is absent from requirements.txt (arrives only transitively via pandas). `tqdm` and `jsonlines` are listed but a repo-wide grep finds no import of either. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml:28) installs from this same unpinned file.
findings.failure_scenario: The receiving lab (or CI, months from now) runs `pip install -r requirements.txt` and the resolver picks a new major of pandas/numpy/anthropic released after delivery; the pipeline crashes mid-run or the anthropic SDK renames a Messages.create parameter and every generation call fails — after the run directory is created and partial paid work is done. Nobody can reconstruct the environment the committed example runs were produced with, because no exact versions were ever recorded (run_manifest.json records config and git commit, not package versions).
findings.recommendation: Adopt a two-file scheme sized for non-engineers: rename requirements.txt to requirements.in (add `numpy`, delete `tqdm` and `jsonlines`), then generate a fully pinned lockfile with `uv pip compile requirements.in -o requirements.txt` (or `pip-compile`). CI and the README setup instructions keep installing from requirements.txt unchanged; contributors only touch requirements.in. Add one CLAUDE.md line: 'to add a dependency, edit requirements.in and rerun uv pip compile'. Optionally record installed versions into run_manifest.json (`importlib.metadata.distributions()`) so every run self-documents its environment.

findings.title: CI merge gate runs only compileall + pytest — no lint, no format check, no type check, no coverage floor; repo has no [tool.ruff] or formatter config at all
findings.evidence: ci.yml's single `smoke` job is checkout → pip install → `python -m compileall` (line 31) → `pytest` (line 34). pyproject.toml contains only `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` — no `[project]`, `[tool.ruff]`, or `[tool.mypy]` (verified via tomllib). The debt compounds until formatter adoption means a repo-wide diff that breaks `git blame` and every open branch; meanwhile genuine bug-pattern lints like B023 ship to main unexamined.

Autofix-first adoption in one PR: (1) add to pyproject.toml:

line-length = 100
target-version = "py312"
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "W", "B", "C4", "SIM", "DTZ"]
ignore = ["E501"]  # formatter owns wrapping
(deliberately exclude C901/PLR complexity rules — wrong gate for non-engineers); (2) run `ruff check --fix . && ruff format .` as a single mechanical commit; (3) add that commit's SHA to a new .git-blame-ignore-revs and document `git config blame.ignoreRevsFile .git-blame-ignore-revs`; (4) append a `lint` job to ci.yml:

and make it a required check alongside smoke; (5) optional pre-commit for those who want it (repos: ruff-pre-commit, hooks: ruff + ruff-format) but never required — CI is the enforcement point. Add a CLAUDE.md policy line: 'run ruff check --fix . && ruff format . before every commit; CI rejects unformatted code'.

findings.title: 69 mypy errors with no mypy config; roughly a third trace to call_claude's flag-dependent union return type poisoning every call site
findings.evidence: shared/api.py:391-401 declares `call_claude(..., return_stop_reason: bool = False, ...) -> str | tuple[str, str | None]`. Every downstream caller that passes the flag unpacks or strips the result, producing ~20 of the 69 errors: five `str-unpack` (dad_pipeline/step2_responses.py:145,171; step3_rewrite.py:58,67; pref_pipeline/run.py:151), eight `arg-type` on parse helpers (sdf_pipeline/layer1_document_types.py:44, layer2_subtypes.py:59, layer5_score.py:80, dad_pipeline/step1_dilemmas.py:620,735, evals/audit_sdf.py:398,418,437), and `union-attr` `.strip()` errors (evals/score_sdf.py:61, score_dad.py:92, sdf_pipeline/layer4_rewrite.py:52-55). Another 11 errors are one line — shared/api.py:230 iterating SDK content blocks without an isinstance(TextBlock) narrow. The repo has no [tool.mypy] section, so none of this is visible to contributors or CI.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor flips a call site to `return_stop_reason=True` (or back) without updating the unpacking — the type system is silent because the union already type-errors everywhere, so the mistake is invisible until runtime: the code crashes AFTER the paid API call returns and BEFORE the result is checkpointed, so `--resume` re-bills that call. The class of bug mypy exists to catch is exactly the one the current signature makes uncheckable.
findings.recommendation:
Three-step gradual adoption: (1) fix the root cause with typing.overload on call_claude — `@overload def call_claude(..., return_stop_reason: Literal[True], ...) -> tuple[str, str | None]` / `@overload ... Literal[False] = ... -> str` — which erases ~20 errors with zero runtime change; (2) fix shared/api.py:230 with `if isinstance(block, TextBlock)` (kills 11 errors) and add the two trivial var annotations (constitution_loader.py:146, audit_sdf.py:265,284,442); (3) add a deliberately narrow config that is green on day one:
[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.12"
files = ["shared", "sdf_pipeline", "dad_pipeline", "pref_pipeline", "evals"]
exclude = ["viewer"]
ignore_missing_imports = true
The remaining ~15 errors live in viewer/ (excluded — 0%-tested Streamlit UI) and a handful of eval edge cases. Add `mypy` as a non-blocking CI step first, flip to required once green for two weeks.

findings.title: claude-code-review.yml prompt does not encode the repo's own PR policies, so the only reviewer most PRs get never checks them; action pinned to mutable @v1 tag
findings.evidence: The review prompt (lines 71-77) asks only for 'Bugs, logic errors... Security issues... Clear violations of guidelines in any relevant CLAUDE.md' and then 'Skip nitpicks'. It never instructs the reviewer to verify the repo's three hard PR requirements from CLAUDE.md: tests must accompany pipeline changes ('a stage without tests is a stage that silently breaks at $50 a run'), the PR body must contain a 'How to test' section (explicitly noted as bypassed by `gh pr create --body`), and prompt-template placeholder changes must update tests/test_prompts_render.py. Per the merge-gate policy, claude[bot]'s approval can satisfy the required review with no human involved — so an approval here IS the merge gate. Both workflows also use `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1` (line 53; claude.yml:35), a mutable tag, and claude-code-review.yml:59 sets `allowed_bots: "*"`.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor opens a PR from a Claude session that changes dad_pipeline/step2_responses.py with no test changes and a template-generated body missing 'How to test'. CI passes (existing tests untouched), the Claude review approves — its prompt told it to look for bugs, not policy — and since claude[bot] approval satisfies the branch-protection review requirement, the PR merges with zero human eyes. The untested stage change breaks the next $10 run. Separately, a compromised @v1 tag would execute attacker code in a job holding the org's CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN.
findings.recommendation: Append a repo-policy block to the prompt in claude-code-review.yml (after line 77): 'Additionally verify, and request changes if violated: (1) any change under shared/, sdf_pipeline/, dad_pipeline/, pref_pipeline/, or evals/ includes corresponding changes under tests/ — check the diff file list; (2) the PR body contains a How to test section with runnable commands (read it with `gh pr view <n> --json body`); (3) if any prompts/ template changed its {placeholders}, tests/test_prompts_render.py changed in the same PR; (4) no stage change checkpoints failed work or re-does completed work on --resume (the checkpoint/resume contract in CLAUDE.md).' Add `Bash(gh pr view:*)` — already allowed — so (2) works. Separately: pin both workflows' `anthropics/claude-code-action` to a full commit SHA with a version comment, and narrow `allowed_bots: "*"` to the specific bots that push (e.g. `claude[bot]`).

Both workflows use mutable anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 (claude-code-review.yml:53, claude.yml:35) with CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN passed in, and allowed_bots: "*" is at line 59. The merge-gate mechanism is corroborated by the project memory (live-verified on PR #31): claude[bot] approval + smoke CI suffices for same-repo merges with no human review, so the failure scenario is mechanically possible. Minor caveat only: "never checks them" is a behavioral prediction — the reviewer could occasionally flag missing tests via the CLAUDE.md clause — but the core claim (policies not encoded in the prompt that constitutes the effective merge gate) holds as stated.

packages = ["shared", "sdf_pipeline", "dad_pipeline", "pref_pipeline", "evals", "viewer"]
Then change the setup docs to `pip install -e .`, delete the sys.path.insert lines from library modules first (safe — they're only imported after an entry point already patched the path), and from entry points last. Keep requires-python in sync with shared/__init__.py's MIN_PYTHON.

A lab running `pip install .` fails for lack of build metadata; running scripts from outside the repo root fails on the cwd-relative default `--config config.yaml` (though the outputs/ and prompts/ trees are correctly anchored to the repo root via __file__), and the import-time path mutation in library modules makes import behavior order-dependent and confuses type checkers/IDEs.
findings.verifier_notes: Verified pyproject.toml has only [tool.pytest.ini_options] (incl. pythonpath=["."]), no [project]/[build-system]/setup.py/setup.cfg, so pip install . cannot yield a usable package; all ten cited sys.path.insert file:line pairs are exact. Two detail corrections: the true mutation count is 23 files (the list omits all of dad_pipeline/ and viewer/, e.g. dad_pipeline/run.py:16, viewer/loader.py:11), and the outputs/ tree is anchored to Path(__file__).parent.parent in all three orchestrators (sdf_pipeline/run.py:34-36, dad_pipeline/run.py:42-44, pref_pipeline/run.py:89-91), not cwd — only the default --config config.yaml is cwd-relative, so running from elsewhere fails fast on config load rather than half-working and writing outputs to the wrong place.

findings.title: Stale root-level working reports and internal references ship with the delivery
findings.evidence: sdf-notebook-port-report.md:3 (repo root, 44KB) states '**Status:** implemented locally on `main`, uncommitted, awaiting review (this report)' — the work has long since merged, so the banner is false in the delivered tree. Its 30KB companion sdf-pipeline-walkthrough.md and git-workflow-guide.md also sit at the root, undocumented by CLAUDE.md's directory map. .env.example:3 says 'Ask Oliver for an API key' and README.md:138 repeats '(ask Oliver)' — an instruction that dead-ends for anyone outside the original team.
findings.failure_scenario: A lab engineer skimming the delivered root reads 'uncommitted, awaiting review' and reasonably concludes the tree is missing pending work, spending time chasing a phantom diff; a new user follows .env.example and has no path to a key. Stale status text at the top level also signals unmaintained docs and taints trust in the accurate ones.
findings.recommendation: Before delivery: move the two SDF design reports into context_docs/ (their content is genuinely valuable history — the belief-implantation rejection rationale) with a one-line 'historical design record, describes the state as of commit 9609e1f' banner replacing the stale status line; move git-workflow-guide.md to a docs/ or .github/ location or fold it into CONTRIBUTING.md; replace 'Ask Oliver' in .env.example:3 and README.md:138 with a role-based instruction ('ask the project maintainer / see the team key-distribution doc').
